subject: BlueHarbor: clarifying hosting & residency options, APAC routing

Subject: Quick follow-up and clarifying questions from today's call

Hi Caroline / Raj — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the right deployment pattern for BlueHarbor: 

Recap (high level):
- Primary constraint: production workloads must reside in the EU (data residency / regulator preference).
- Secondary requirement: APAC presence for DR and lower-latency access for a subset of customers.
- Non-prod/dev can tolerate hosted cloud options.

Questions to help us recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC:
1) For production: are you prescriptive about a single EU region (e.g., eu-west) or would multi-EU-region active/active be required?
2) Expected steady-state qps (inference requests/sec) and 95th p95 latency target for production (token-level latency or end-to-end)?
3) Any mandatory KMS/HSM provider or key policies we should account for?
4) Procurement timing: do you have an estimated go-live window (Q1 2027, etc.) and internal procurement/PO lead?

Next steps I propose: Marcus to propose a short architecture options doc (private VPC + APAC fallback, hosted dev flow, cost/latency tradeoffs), and then schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with your infra/security team. I attached a draft SOW and our SOC2 statement for initial review.

Attachments: [Attachment: blueharbor-sow-draft.pdf (PDF)] [Attachment: redwood-soc2-statement.pdf (PDF)]

Thanks — Jasmine

Thanks Jasmine — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Production must be hosted within the EU. We prefer a single primary EU region (we're standardizing on eu-west) but we may need cross-region replication for failover.
- APAC: this would be primarily DR/fallback and lower-latency reads for APAC customers; write workloads must stay in the EU.
- Target volume: initial POC ~200 rps, production expected 800-1,200 rps within 6 months. P95 latency target is <= 300ms end-to-end for the inference call (we understand token-level variation).
- KMS: we use Azure Key Vault currently for customer-managed keys; we need compatibility or a clear flow to integrate our KMS for encryption-at-rest keys.
- Timeline: procurement kicking off mid-December; preferred go-live window is Feb–Mar 2027.

Please send the architecture options and any notes on cross-region routing/failover. Also please attach the SOC2 and any network onboarding checklist for a Private VPC.

-Caroline

On Tue, 2026-11-17 at 09:42, Caroline Hayes wrote:
> Production must be hosted within the EU...

Hi Caroline / Raj — thanks for the details. Below are three pragmatic options (tradeoffs included) based on your constraints and traffic profile: 

Option A — Private VPC (recommended for prod):
- Description: Private control plane, customer-managed VPC peered to Redwood serving plane in eu-west. All production inference served from eu-west; keys remain under your KMS (Azure Key Vault) via our KMS bridge.
- APAC: deploy read-only inference pool in ap-southeast-1 for DR/low-latency reads. Cross-region routing handled by our smart routing policy: write requests are routed to eu-west; reads can be served from APAC pool with KV prefix validation to ensure consistency.
- Pros: strongest data residency and control, KMS integration, SLA-backed capacity.
- Cons: higher setup time and reserved capacity cost.
- Latency estimate: eu-west to EU customers: 40–120ms p50; APAC reads from ap-southeast: 160–260ms p95 (depends on network egress).

Option B — Dedicated reserved capacity in EU + Hosted dev: 
- Description: Dedicated GPU pools in eu-west for prod; non-prod/dev uses Redwood Hosted API in EU. KMS via bring-your-key pattern available, but keys held in Redwood HSM unless we run private KMS bridge (adds ops work).
- Pros: faster ramp than Private VPC, predictable throughput.
- Cons: slightly less isolation than Private VPC; KMS flow requires signing controls.

Option C — Hosted API (not recommended for prod given residency constraint):
- Description: Fully hosted in EU; simpler onboarding but less control over network and KMS integration.

Next steps we propose:
- I will send a short architecture appendix (attached) that diagrams Option A+B and outlines network onboarding steps for Private VPC (peerings, permitted IP ranges, and KMS handshake).
- Schedule 60-min technical deep dive with your infra/security and our infra/SE team — propose Wed 2026-11-24 or Thu 2026-11-25 (we're flexible).

Attachments: [Attachment: architecture-choices-appendix.md]

—Marcus
